Title: Departed workforce account remains enabled
Criteria: Departed workforce identities must be disabled at the approved termination time, active sessions revoked, and downstream application access checked.
Condition: USR-005 has an HR end date of 31 July 2026 but remains Enabled on the 24 August 2026 review date. The last simulated sign-in was 4 August 2026, after the employment end date.
Cause: The manual leaver process has no complete system checklist, timed trigger, independent validation, or exception escalation.
Risk: A former-user identity may access Microsoft 365 or connected applications, expose business data, or support fraud and unauthorized activity.
Recommendation: Disable the identity immediately, revoke sessions, review post-end-date activity, remove downstream access, transfer owned resources, and independently validate closure.
Validation_Step: Check HR database status against identity store status; verify session revocation logs.

Title: MFA is not centrally enforced for standard workforce identities
Criteria: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) must be centrally enforced for all active workforce identities accessing corporate environments.
Condition: A sample of 10 out of 56 active standard workforce identities shows that central conditional access policies do not mandate MFA for standard logins.
Cause: MFA configuration relies on legacy per-user activation instead of modern, tenant-wide Conditional Access enforcement policies.
Risk: Absence of mandatory MFA drastically increases susceptibility to credential stuffing, phishing, and unauthorized tenant access.
Recommendation: Deploy a tenant-wide Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all standard workforce identities.
Validation_Step: Review Entra ID Conditional Access policy configurations and verify user MFA registration status reports.

Title: Expired guest access remains enabled
Criteria: External guest access must be bounded by an explicit expiration date and disabled immediately upon contract termination.
Condition: Guest accounts GST-002 and GST-004 remain active and enabled despite their documented assignment timelines having expired.
Cause: The organization lacks automated lifecycle management or periodic access reviews for external business guest tenants.
Risk: Persistent external access allows former partners or contractors continuous entry to shared corporate repositories and communication channels.
Recommendation: Revoke access for GST-002 and GST-004 immediately, and establish automated lifecycle expiration for all external guests.
Validation_Step: Inspect active external user directory logs and cross-reference with procurement/contract expiration files.

Title: Service identities permit interactive sign-in and one lacks ownership
Criteria: Non-human service identities must block interactive sign-ins, and every active service principle must map to a clear business owner.
Condition: SVC-001 and SVC-004 accept direct user/password interactive logins, and SVC-004 lacks an assigned operational department owner.
Cause: Service accounts were provisioned using standard user account templates rather than dedicated, non-interactive service principal structures.
Risk: Interactive service accounts run a higher risk of credential exposure and malicious exploitation without accountability for systemic changes.
Recommendation: Convert accounts to non-interactive service principles, rotate credentials, and explicitly document ownership for SVC-004.
Validation_Step: Review sign-in log types for service accounts to verify only non-interactive tokens are processed.

Title: Mover retained former-role administration
Criteria: Mover access must match the new role, and former-role access must be removed within one business day of the effective change.
Condition: USR-007 moved from Support Lead to Finance Analyst on 1 August 2026 but retains Zendesk Administrator access. The target Finance Analyst role permits Stripe Read and no Zendesk administration.
Cause: Role changes grant new access without automatically comparing and removing prior-role permissions.
Risk: Excessive customer-support administration can expose ticket data, permit unauthorized changes, and weaken separation of responsibility.
Recommendation: Remove Zendesk Administrator access, validate the remaining Finance permissions, and implement an old-role versus new-role difference check for every mover.
Validation_Step: Check current access privileges for USR-007 across Zendesk and verify historical HR role modification logs.

Title: Finance permissions create a separation-of-duties conflict
Criteria: Financial control structures must strictly enforce Separation of Duties (SoD) between transaction initiation and approval roles.
Condition: USR-008 possesses concurrent operational authority to both create banking vendor entries and approve final vendor invoices.
Cause: Role-based access controls within the financial application do not incorporate toxic combination rule validation.
Risk: Unmitigated SoD conflicts in financial systems increase the risk of unauthorized disbursements, internal fraud, or accounting errors.
Recommendation: Revoke vendor creation access from USR-008, re-assigning it to an independent operations handler to satisfy SoD mandates.
Validation_Step: Execute a privilege analysis within the financial enterprise resource planning (ERP) system to verify role isolation.

Title: Standing privileged access has no quarterly review evidence
Criteria: Privileged access must be least-privileged, reviewed quarterly, and time-limited where supported.
Condition: Four active workforce identities have standing privileged roles, and no previous access-review date is recorded. Two identities hold Global Administrator access in the simulated dataset.
Cause: Privileged roles are assigned directly and have no recurring recertification or eligible-activation workflow.
Risk: Unnecessary or persistent privilege increases the effect of credential theft, misuse, error, and compromised daily-work accounts.
Recommendation: Review every privileged role, reduce broad administration, separate daily and admin identities, and plan eligible time-limited activation with strong MFA and approval where supported.
Validation_Step: Verify active tenant administrators via control pane and cross-reference with missing historical access audit signatures.

Title: Stale enabled identities lack documented owner decisions
Criteria: Identities that remain inactive or stale for longer than 90 days must be reviewed and systematically flagged for deactivation or owner justification.
Condition: SVC-004, GST-002, GST-003, and USR-013 have zero recorded login activity for over 90 days but remain fully active and enabled.
Cause: There is no automated alerting script or scheduled operational playbook to catch and remediate inactive accounts.
Risk: Stale enabled accounts serve as prime vectors for target exploitation since unauthorized logons are less likely to be noticed immediately.
Recommendation: Formally query the respective owners for business justification; disable accounts immediately if no validation is returned.
Validation_Step: Audit last interactive and non-interactive sign-in metadata fields across the active user index.

Title: Joiner-mover-leaver governance is not formalized
Criteria: The Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) identity lifecycle must be fully governed by formalized, reviewed, and approved operating procedures.
Condition: No authoritative standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation exists to dictate the lifecycle triggers between HR and IT teams.
Cause: The identity provisioning and deprovisioning operations have grown organically without a formalized corporate governance framework.
Risk: Ad-hoc lifecycle practices yield systemic operational gaps, directly causing errors like orphaned accounts or lingering admin rights.
Recommendation: Draft, ratify, and execute an official Joiner-Mover-Leaver lifecycle SOP aligning HR events with technical IAM controls.
Validation_Step: Verify the publication and cross-departmental signature of the finalized JML lifecycle governance policy.

Title: Emergency administrative access is not defined or tested
Criteria: Emergency administrative accounts ('break-glass' accounts) must be formally defined, excluded from standard MFA loops, and tested annually.
Condition: The tenant does not contain designated emergency-only admin privileges, and no disaster recovery validation drills have been performed.
Cause: Emergency recovery planning has been deferred in favor of standard operational administrative engineering tracks.
Risk: Systemic configuration failures or external service outages impacting standard MFA paths could completely lock out all available administrators.
Recommendation: Create two dedicated cloud-only break-glass administrative accounts with highly complex passwords stored in secure physical vaults.
Validation_Step: Verify existence of non-interactive cloud administrative accounts and inspect the physical security log documentation.
